title: Happy Birthday, Rafael Philip Trunx C. Ybañez
dek: BNCHS SSLG greeted its President and recognized the steady leadership, patience and care he brings to the student body.
body: BNCHS SSLG celebrated President Rafael Philip Trunx C. Ybañez, recognizing the responsibility involved in leading the student body and the steadiness he brings to the council. The greeting emphasized courage, patience, focus and genuine concern for learners.
The council also thanked him for sustained service to the school community and for guiding the organization through its programs and reporting cycle. The post was prepared by Regina Faye I. Tambole.

title: World Teachers' Month: a salute to BNCHS educators
dek: The SSLG honored teachers as mentors, second parents and champions of student growth during World Teachers' Month.
facts: Gratitude for mentorship, patience and support
Regina Faye I. Tambole & Lheianna Laureene Montalban
body: For World Teachers' Month, BNCHS SSLG addressed the educators who guide students both academically and personally. The message described teachers as mentors, second parents and supporters of students' dreams, highlighting the patience required to teach lessons inside and beyond the classroom.
The greeting thanked BNCHS teachers for creating an environment where students are expected not only to learn but to grow. The post credits Regina Faye I. Tambole and Lheianna Laureene Montalban.

title: BNCHS SSLG marks the 34th Family Day
dek: A school-community greeting celebrated family as an anchor through challenges and a source of strength behind students' dreams.
facts: Family as an anchor, source of strength and support
body: The SSLG joined the celebration of BNCHS's 34th Family Day with a message about the role of family in keeping people grounded through difficulties and supporting their ambitions. The post encouraged the school community to value shared moments, laughter and quiet forms of support.

As a community-facing entry, the post records the learner government's role beyond meetings and programs: it also participates in school-wide observances that reinforce relationships among learners and families.

title: Verse of the Week: Isaiah 41:10
dek: The weekly reflection centered on courage, reassurance and strength in the face of uncertainty and heavy burdens.
facts: Courage, reassurance and trust amid uncertainty
body: The week's reflection used Isaiah 41:10 to address fear, uncertainty and overwhelming circumstances. The SSLG's message emphasized that people do not have to carry difficult situations alone and can draw strength and reassurance from faith.
The post framed the verse around peace, perseverance and trust—encouraging students to remain steady when responsibilities or problems feel heavy.

title: Accomplishment Report 05: First-Term record
dek: The fifth accomplishment report summarized a productive first term focused on student engagement and community involvement.
facts: Student engagement, community involvement, environmental initiatives, talent showcases and competitions
body: Accomplishment Report 05 closed the first-term reporting cycle by describing the term as productive and focused on student engagement and community involvement. The council pointed to environmental initiatives, talent showcases and student competitions as part of the term's work.

Placed beside the First-Term SOLGA in the archive, the report functions as a public accountability record: it gives learners a permanent reference for the work the council says it completed during the term.

body: BNCHS SSLG reported a successful turnout for the First-Term State of the Learner Government Address held on September 24. The gathering was conducted under the SSLG's by-laws and was used to present accomplishment reports, financial updates and plans for the rest of the school year.

The recap thanked attendees for participating in the accountability session. Keeping the recap alongside the event advisory lets students see both the planned program and the council's record that the program was carried out.

The program was presented as an open reporting platform for accomplishment reports, transparent updates and the SSLG's game plan. Those details make the post an important governance record rather than a simple event reminder.

Super Vicious was listed with Cristopher Musico, Jack Calimpusan, Cart Juanite, Ivan Salindato, Zinxuss Clare Gallaron and Terrence Regino. body: ATRAKA 2026 concluded on Day 3 with several strands of the festival coming together. The SSLG recap highlighted continued Bamboo Booth activity, Laro ng Lahi, the grand awarding for e-sports champions and a clean-up drive after the celebration.

The final-day post closed the festival sequence and thanked participants. In this archive, the Day 1, Day 2 and Day 3 recaps remain separate so the flow of the event can be followed rather than collapsed into one summary.

The post positioned the second day as one of the most competition-heavy parts of the festival, bridging the setup-focused first day and the awarding and closing activities on Day 3.

dek: The first day focused on final preparations, the opening of booths and the start of the festival atmosphere.
facts: Final preparations, booth opening and festival kickoff

The Bamboo Booth was among the featured activities, while the post also previewed the games and competitions that would define the following days.

Published prices were ₱89 for the photobooth, ₱30 for an extra strip and ₱50 for a keychain. The post was credited to Prince Honniel Micabalo and Regina Faye I. Tambole.

The published registration links were forms.gle/WM4gktiz9Seep2S59 for Laro ng Lahi, forms.gle/HtogUkVYpypLCWpJ7 for MLBB and forms.gle/HcnKcKM6LHnuFYfT7 for CODM. Prize-pool information was referenced in the earlier activity posts.

title: Laro ng Lahi: four days of Filipino games
dek: The SSLG invited teams to free Laro ng Lahi activities from August 18–21, 3:00–5:00 PM, in front of the Principal's Office.
facts: In front of the Principal's Office
body: Laro ng Lahi was scheduled from August 18 to 21, from 3:00 to 5:00 PM, in front of the Principal's Office. Registration was free and was handled through the SSLG Office.

The announcement allowed 20 students per team per day and said five games would be played each day, turning the traditional-games activity into a four-day ATRAKA program rather than a single exhibition.

title: ATRAKA E-Sports: Call of Duty Mobile registration
dek: CODM teams were invited to register at the SSLG Office for ₱50 per player, with full squads required.
facts: Members from different ATRAKA groups may form a team
Full squads only; solo registrations not accepted
Luisa Galindo & Regina Faye I. Tambole
body: For Call of Duty Mobile, the SSLG opened ATRAKA registration at the SSLG Office at ₱50 per player. Players from different ATRAKA groups were allowed to form a team.

The key restriction was that only full squads would be accepted; individual or solo registrations were not allowed. The post framed the tournament around coordination, rotations and competitive team play.

title: ATRAKA E-Sports: Mobile Legends registration
dek: MLBB teams were invited to register at the SSLG Office for ₱50 per player, with complete five-player rosters required.
facts: Members from different ATRAKA groups may form a team
Luisa Galindo & Regina Faye I. Tambole
body: The Mobile Legends: Bang Bang tournament used the same ₱50-per-player registration fee and accepted sign-ups at the SSLG Office. Players from different ATRAKA groups could combine into one team.

Teams had to register as a complete five-player roster, and solo registrations were not accepted. The announcement emphasized shot-calling, macro play and team synergy as the qualities the tournament would test.

facts: Relevance 25%; Creativity & Originality 20%; Visual Appeal & Composition 30%; Craftsmanship & Neatness 25%
Originality & Choreography 30; Timing & Coordination 25; Theme & Creativity 25; Overall Impact 20
Regina Faye I. Tambole; Luisa Galindo; Lheianna Montalban
body: Nutrition Month opened three different ways for students to participate under the theme 'Nutrisyon at Kalikasan, Ating Pangalagaan!': Poster Making, a Dance Video Competition and a Nutrition Quiz Bowl.

Poster Making was scored on relevance to the theme (25%), creativity and originality (20%), visual appeal and composition (30%), and craftsmanship and neatness (25%). Dance Video entries were scored on originality and choreography (30), timing and coordination (25), theme and creativity (25), and overall impact (20). Registration used forms.gle/bRYbxiHPRFqcPthr7 and closed July 19.
The creative committee named in the post was Regina Faye I. Tambole, Luisa Galindo and Lheianna Montalban.

facts: Dedication, outgoing personality and positive team energy
body: The SSLG greeted Treasurer Aira Omillo and highlighted both her dedication to her role and the energy she contributes to the team. The post described her as bubbly and outgoing, noting that those qualities make collective work more enjoyable.
The greeting encouraged her to keep that positive character while continuing to do her best in service.

title: Kompre Reels 01: Committee Induction Day
dek: A reel captured the first introductions and shared goals that marked the start of a stronger, more unified SSLG committee community.
facts: Passionate students came together to serve, lead and build a more unified SSLG
body: Kompre Reels 01 documented Committee Induction Day as a moment when students came together ready to serve, lead and make an impact. The reel moved from first introductions toward the shared goals of the new committee community.
The council described the gathering as the foundation of a stronger and more unified SSLG, making the reel a visual companion to the formal Committee Induction photo post.

title: Committee Induction Day formally begins committee service
dek: The official photo post described committee membership as a chance to shape, organize and strengthen systems that serve the student body.
facts: Members actively shape, organize and strengthen systems serving the student body
body: The Committee Induction Day post explained why committee service matters: members are given a direct role in shaping student life and creating a more engaging, inclusive and impactful school experience.

The induction marked the formal beginning of committee responsibilities. The post said student leaders were expected to do more than participate—they were expected to help shape, organize and strengthen the systems that serve the student body. The original post contains a multi-photo carousel documenting the induction.
